newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso weakened by devaluation scare.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso weakened by devaluation scare.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed weaker on Thursday as the market continued to be haunted by fears of a devaluation, traders said.
Despite raising its overnight borrowing rate to 32 percent on Thursday, the Central Bank had to sell millions of dollars.
The peso ended at 26.401 to the dollar from 26.40, with volume lower at $619 million from Wednesday's $1.02 billion.
Some banks were trying to arbitrage against the Central Bank, buying dollars from it for next-day delivery and selling to the market for settlement today, traders said.
In this way, they were able to get more pesos which they placed overnight with the Central Bank.
That stopped the Central Bank from selling dollars to those banks, forcing them to buy dollars at higher rates. The peso therefore went to an intraday-low of 26.403 pesos.
With the peso slipping, offshore funds became panicky and closed their positions, traders said.
One trader estimated the Central Bank may have sold $350 million at 26.40 pesos, of which $25 million were at 26.388.
